methodology.title: How we assess
methodology.subtitle: Every score traces to a documented source.
methodology.intro: Rihal Aptitude measures behavioral fit for a role family — not job knowledge or general intelligence. Each competency traces to an O*NET work style or cited Big Five literature, and every result decomposes fit → competency → trait → source.
methodology.chain: Role family → O*NET work styles + Big Five trait literature → target competency profile. A candidate's IPIP-NEO-120 traits and situational-judgement responses are compared against that target to produce a fit score and community percentiles.
methodology.norms: Community percentiles use the Johnson IPIP-NEO research dataset (Western-skewed, 2001–2011). Fit-to-role does not depend on it; percentiles are a secondary reference. Local validity comes from the calibration loop over time.
methodology.construct: The assessment is built to recognized standards: the IPIP-NEO-120 measures the Big Five (Five-Factor) model; competency targets derive from O*NET work styles and peer-reviewed trait–performance literature. Construction and use follow the AERA/APA/NCME Standards for Educational and Psychological Testing and the SIOP Principles for the Validation and Use of Personnel Selection Procedures.
methodology.limits: This is a behavioral-fit signal, not a verdict — it does not measure job knowledge or general cognitive ability, and it never decides. Self-report instruments are sensitive to context and response style; the community norms are demographically skewed and used only as a secondary reference. A computed fit score is decision support for a human reviewer, who records the call.
methodology.decomposition: Every fit score breaks down into competency → trait facet → cited source, so a reviewer can see why a number is what it is. We surface the evidence trail other tools hide behind a single proprietary number.

roleProfiles.noSjt: No SJT items. They’re optional — add one if this role needs a scenario.
roleProfiles.approveNeedsCompetency: Add at least one competency before approving.

roleProfiles.editSubtitle: Revise this draft. Approving it activates this version.

results.radarSubtitle: Candidate score against the role’s target for each competency.
results.breakdownSubtitle: Each competency rolls up from trait facets and traces to its source.
results.traitSubtitle: The five Big Five domains and their facets, as community percentiles.
results.sjtSubtitle: Judgement signal from scenario responses, scored against the role’s key.

calibration.title: Calibration
calibration.subtitle: Validate role bands against real hire outcomes over time. Every suggestion is advisory — you approve each change.
calibration.captureSubtitle: Attach post-hire outcomes to scored candidates. This is the data the calibration loop learns from.
calibration.captureEmpty: No scored candidates yet. Outcomes can be attached once candidates complete an assessment and a result is computed.
calibration.postHireNote: These accrue over time — leave any unknown for now.
calibration.nonHiredNote: Post-hire signals only apply to a hired candidate.
calibration.saveError: Couldn’t save the outcome. Try again.
calibration.reportSubtitle: For a role version with enough recorded outcomes, see whether predicted fit and each competency tracked real success.
calibration.noRoles: No approved or active role versions yet.
calibration.insufficient: Needs {need} outcomes to calibrate — {have} recorded so far. Keep capturing outcomes to unlock this role.
calibration.neverGenerated: No report yet for this role. Generate one once enough outcomes are recorded.
calibration.fitChartSubtitle: Each point is one hired candidate. A positive trend means higher predicted fit went with better outcomes.
calibration.signalSubtitle: How each competency’s score related to observed success, and an advisory band direction.
calibration.advisoryNote: Suggestions are advisory. Applying one means creating a NEW role-profile version with the adjusted band — the system never changes a band on its own.
calibration.adverseSubtitle: Advance rates by role family, with a 4/5ths-rule flag for groups selected well below the highest rate.
calibration.adverseEmpty: No decisions recorded yet — the monitor populates as managers record decisions.
calibration.adverseCapped: Showing the {shown} most recent of {total} decided candidates — rates are partial.
calibration.adverseDemographicNote: Protected-class demographics are not collected by design (PDPL data-minimization), so this is a structural selection-rate monitor, not an EEO adverse-impact study.
